review_basis: Agent-reviewed labels using the user-approved transition-aware interviewer rubric; user spot-checked and approved freezing this draft as v1.
action_derivation: next_action is derived from max relevance per query: 3=direct_follow_up, 2=bridged_follow_up, 1=clarify_or_narrow, 0=reset_or_redirect.

rubric.3: Very suitable as a natural next question. Can be a direct deep dive or a high-value horizontal expansion grounded in the candidate stated module, responsibility, goal, or problem.
rubric.2: Relevant and usable with an explainable transition, but not the best direct next question or needs a short bridge from the interviewer.
rubric.1: Topically related but the current answer lacks enough anchor. The interviewer should clarify, narrow, or request a concrete module/process before asking this atom.
rubric.0: Irrelevant, obvious topic jump, or only based on generic AI-project association. The interviewer should ignore this atom and redirect/reset.

next_action_definitions.direct_follow_up: Top candidates include a score-3 atom; interviewer can directly ask a knowledge follow-up based on the atom.
next_action_definitions.bridged_follow_up: Best candidates are score-2; interviewer can use the atom after a short natural bridge.
next_action_definitions.clarify_or_narrow: Only score-1 candidates exist; interviewer should first narrow, clarify, or ask the candidate to make the answer concrete instead of directly using an atom.
next_action_definitions.reset_or_redirect: All candidates are score-0; interviewer should ignore these atoms and redirect to the role mainline or recover the previous question.

notes: A score of 1 or 0 does not mean the atom itself is poor; it means the atom is not suitable as the direct next question in the current dialogue state.
When all retrieved candidates are 0 or 1, the interviewer should not force a knowledge-atom follow-up. It should clarify, narrow, reset, or redirect first.
The committed atom snapshot freezes the published AI-model atom corpus used for v1 scoring.
